subject: Archaeology
title: Fashion and Beauty in Ancient Egypt
description: A quick, practical guide to Fashion and Beauty in Ancient Egypt.

hook.text: Both men and women in ancient Egypt wore eyeliner. It was not fashion — it was medicine.

buildup.text: Kohl eyeliner contained lead salts that boosted immune cells in the eyes, reducing infection rates.

discovery.text: Wigs were universal among the wealthy. They shaved their heads for cleanliness and wore wigs for style.

twist.text: Linen clothing was see-through by design. Modesty standards were very different from modern ones.

climax.text: Perfume cones made of animal fat sat on top of wigs, slowly melting and releasing scent throughout the day.

punchline.text: Egyptian beauty was part vanity, part chemistry, and part public health.

quiz.question: Why did Egyptians wear kohl eyeliner?
options: It was required by religious law for all citizens
Lead salts in kohl boosted immune cells and reduced eye infections
It was a symbol of mourning worn after funerals

details.summary: Ancient Egyptians valued personal appearance, using cosmetics, wigs, jewelry, and fine linen garments. Kohl eyeliner served both aesthetic and medical purposes by reducing sun glare and fighting eye infections. Elaborate beauty rituals reflected social status and religious devotion.
details.whyItMatters: Archaeological beauty artifacts reveal Egyptian social hierarchies and cultural values. Modern cosmetic science has confirmed that some Egyptian formulations had genuine antibacterial properties, linking ancient aesthetics to practical health.
takeaways: Kohl eyeliner had both cosmetic and antibacterial functions
Wigs, jewelry, and clothing indicated social status
Beauty rituals were tied to religious and social identity

faq.question: Why did ancient Egyptians wear wigs?
faq.answer: Wigs protected shaved heads from the sun and lice, displayed wealth and status, and served ritual purposes. Elaborate wigs made from human hair or plant fibers were found in tombs. Both men and women wore wigs, with styles changing across dynasties.

faq.question: Did Egyptian kohl actually protect eyes from infection?
faq.answer: Modern chemical analysis shows that lead-based kohl compounds stimulated the immune system's nitric oxide response, fighting bacterial eye infections common near the Nile. Egyptians may have developed this cosmetic specifically for its protective health benefits.
